extraction.name: Geometry3K
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark of 3,002 SAT-style geometry problems collected from two high-school textbooks, covering diverse geometric shapes and problem goals, with dense annotations in formal language for both problem text and diagrams.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from two popular textbooks for high school students across grades 6-12 by two online digital libraries (McGraw-Hill, Geometryonline). Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collected each problem with its problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer. Each problem was also labeled with the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Geometry problems from two popular high school textbooks (grades 6-12) available through two online digital libraries: McGraw-Hill and Geometryonline. Each problem includes problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collected each problem with its problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer. Each problem was labeled with corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes. Annotators were filtered based on performance requirements (time limits applied).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) referenced via footnote 4
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotators who did not satisfy time requirements were filtered out. Human performance was evaluated: overall accuracy of 56.9% compared to random guess of 25%; human experts achieved 90.9% accuracy.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators with undergraduate degrees; additionally, dozens of graduates majoring in science or engineering evaluated human expert performance.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: RetinaNet (object detector for diagram symbols and text regions), MathPix (OCR tool for textual content recognition), Hough Transformation (for geometry primitive extraction), BART (semantic text parser for comparison).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to SAT-style geometry problems from two high-school textbooks covering grades 6-12, and existing geometry datasets are either small in scale or not publicly available. The limited scale of geometry datasets weakens highly data-driven methods.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset supports geometry problem solving, which is an essential subject in high-school education for the development of students' abstract thinking and logical reasoning skills.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training, validation, and testing of geometry problem solving algorithms, particularly for symbolic reasoning and interpretable problem solving. It is divided into train, validation, and test sets with a 0.7:0.1:0.2 ratio.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and evaluation baselines are publicly released to promote follow-up work in the geometry domain. The project with code and data is available at a dedicated website.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Problems were manually collected and annotated with problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, correct answer, problem goal, geometry shapes, and dense formal language descriptions. Data was split into train, validation, and test sets.
